questions.skill: Describe the overall pattern and striking deviations in the context of the data
questions.prompt: The dot plot shows how many hours students slept last night. Describe the overall pattern. Which value stands apart, and what might explain it?
questions.prompt_markup:
The dot plot shows how many hours students slept last night.
Describe the overall pattern. Which value stands apart, and what might explain it?
questions.correct_answer: Most students slept 7 to 9 hours, clustering around 8 hours. One student slept only 4 hours, which stands apart; a reasonable explanation is that the student stayed up late, was sick, or had an early trip.
questions.grading_note: Must name 4 hours as the value that stands apart; any reasonable context explanation is correct

figure.description: Dot plot titled "Hours of sleep last night", number line from 3 to 10. Dots per value: 4: 1, 7: 2, 8: 6, 9: 5, 10: 1.

choices.text: The times are spread evenly from 5 to 30 minutes.

questions.correct_answer: Most students take 5 to 10 minutes; a few who live farther away take 25 to 30 minutes.

questions.skill: Describe the overall pattern and striking deviations in the context of the data
questions.prompt: The histogram shows the ages of people at a youth soccer game. Describe the overall pattern. Which ages stand apart, and who might they be?
questions.prompt_markup:
The histogram shows the ages of people at a youth soccer game.
Describe the overall pattern. Which ages stand apart, and who might they be?
questions.correct_answer: Most people are 0 to 19 years old (the young players). There are no people aged 20 to 29. A few people are 30 to 49; they are probably parents, coaches, or referees.
questions.grading_note: Must describe the cluster of young ages and name the 30–49 ages as standing apart, with a reasonable explanation

figure.description: Histogram (x-axis "Ages of people at a youth soccer game", y-axis "People"). 0–9: 6, 10–19: 9, 20–29: 0, 30–39: 3, 40–49: 1.

sections.skill: Compare the patterns of two distributions

questions.skill: Compare the patterns of two distributions
questions.prompt: Describe how the two distributions differ in context.
questions.prompt_markup: Describe how the two distributions differ in context.
questions.correct_answer: Class A's scores cluster from 7 to 9 (center about 8). Class B's scores cluster from 4 to 6 (center about 5). Class A typically scored about 3 points higher; the spreads are similar, and the plots overlap only at 6.
questions.grading_note: Must compare the centers in context; mentioning spread or overlap is a plus

figure.description: [1] Dot plot titled "Class A quiz scores", number line from 2 to 10. Dots per value: 6: 1, 7: 3, 8: 4, 9: 2. [2] Dot plot titled "Class B quiz scores", number line from 2 to 10. Dots per value: 3: 1, 4: 2, 5: 4, 6: 3.

sections.skill: Describe patterns and deviations in scatter plots in context

questions.skill: Describe patterns and deviations in scatter plots in context
questions.prompt: The scatter plot shows savings over several weeks. Describe the overall pattern and the point that does not fit.
questions.prompt_markup:
The scatter plot shows savings over several weeks.
Describe the overall pattern and the point that does not fit.
questions.correct_answer: Savings grow steadily week by week (a positive, linear pattern of about $7 to $9 per week). The point (6, 20) does not fit; savings dropped that week, perhaps because money was spent.
questions.grading_note: Must describe the upward trend and name (6, 20)

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from 0 to 8 and y from 0 to 70. x-axis label "Weeks", y-axis label "Savings ($)". Points: (1, 20), (2, 28), (3, 35), (4, 41), (5, 50), (6, 20), (7, 64).
